title.narrative: Provision of integrated lifesaving nutrition services in hard-to-reach areas of Qansaxdheere District through community-based preventive nutrition interventions.

description.narrative: ltpgtSOVA will implement a 12-month nutrition project across the five villages of Abag-Deere, Al-Amin, Al-Cadaala, Doodaya, and Esow in Qansaxdheere District to reduce malnutrition among children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLWs). The project will target 9,600 direct individuals (2,600Women, 3200Girls, 3400 Boys and 400 men). The project will align with Somalia’s IMAM and MIYCAN guidelines and will be delivered in close coordination with the MoH, community leaders, and Area-Based Coordination groups. Standardized Nutrition Cluster monitoring and evaluation tools will be applied to ensure quality, consistency, and accountability. Throughout the project, targeted mapping and inclusive strategies will actively engage marginalized and minority groups, ensuring their meaningful participation and representation. Data will be disaggregated by age, gender, disability, and minority status to monitor inclusion and outcomes. Recruitment will prioritize minority staff to reflect community diversity and enhance program relevance.lt/pgtltpgtCHWs will be trained to conduct routine household-level nutrition screening for children under five and PLWs. This will be supplemented by Family MUAC screening led by caregivers and quarterly mass MUAC and oedema screening campaigns. CHWs will refer children with moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) to TSFP and severe acute malnutrition (SAM) cases to OTPs or stabilization centers managed by partners. CHWs will follow up with referred households to reinforce IYCF messages, monitor progress, and provide counseling support at home. IYCF behavior change efforts will be scaled through 60 group education sessions, 55 care groups, 20 cooking demonstrations, and one-on-one counseling for 2,340 caregivers. Cooking sessions will showcase practical, nutritious recipes like Tom Brown porridge and promote the “One Egg Per Day” initiative.ltbrgtMicronutrient powder (MNP) supplementation will be a key component to address micronutrient deficiencies among young children and PLWs. SOVA will distribute MNP sachets to 1,680 children aged 6–23 months during routine household visits and group sessions, with caregivers receiving training on correct usage and adherence supported through follow-up visits. Concurrently, 760 pregnant and lactating women will receive MNP supplementation paired with tailored maternal nutrition counseling. This dual approach will help reduce anemia, improve nutrient intake, and support healthy growth and development for both children and mothers.ltbrgtTo support vulnerable households with children under five or PLW, SOVA will implement a conditional voucher program distributing USD 60 vouchers redeemable for nutrient-dense foods, two live chickens, and five kilograms of poultry feed. Eligibility will be decided through transparent, community-led processes. Beneficiaries must participate in IYCF education sessions and cooking demonstrations to reinforce behavior change. CHWs and MTMSG members will verify participation through home visits, provide counseling, and promote improved nutrition and hygiene practices. Protection principles such as Do No Harm, confidentiality, and gender inclusion will be integrated, supported by accessible feedback mechanisms and mapped referral pathways for GBV and child protection concerns.lt/pgtltpgtA comprehensive CFM will be implemented to collect around 280 entries through feedback desks, suggestion boxes, and verbal reports to CHWs and MTMSG members. Community sensitization activities using Somali-language materials will increase awareness on safe reporting related to PSEA, PDAD, GBV, and child protection. Five referral pathways—one per village—will link community members to health, protection, legal, and psychosocial services. Community-based protection committees will strengthen the capacity to identify and respond to protection risks, reinforce complaints mechanisms, and prioritize inclusion of women, persons with disabilities, youth, and minority clans.ltbrgtlt/pgt
